result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers keep the body and headline spacing as they are, avoid new assets and name specific strengths, so they score about the same on the rubric. A makes one useful change: switching the body size from 17px to 1.0625rem looks identical at default settings but lets the text follow the visitor's browser font-size setting. It also checks contrast concretely, and its figure of about 6:1 is correct. B notices the same unit issue but turns it down for a weak reason, and its contrast note is vaguer ('readable'). | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers find the stylesheet sound, keep the body and h1 metrics, add no assets, and name specific strengths such as the measure, tabular-nums and muted-text contrast. A changes nothing and offers an optional text-wrap tweak. B makes one rendering-neutral px-to-rem change for accessibility, gives a reason for it, and correctly puts the contrast at about 6:1. Both approaches are defensible under 'only change what needs changing.'
